record.original_question: Is the following conjecture true? Conjecture A88 ([S11h]). Let k and l be positive integers. If (ln + 1) |(kn+ln kn ) for all suﬃciently large positive integers n, then each prime factor of k divides l. In other words, if k has a prime factor not dividing l then there are infinitely many positive integers n such that (ln + 1) ∤ (kn+ln kn ) .

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $k$ and $\ell$ be positive integers. Prove or disprove: if $(\ell n+1)\mid \binom{kn+\ell n}{kn}$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $n$, then every prime divisor of $k$ also divides $\ell$. Equivalently, show that whenever $k$ has a prime factor that does not divide $\ell$, there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $(\ell n+1)\nmid \binom{kn+\ell n}{kn}$.
